facts.raw_span: an 18-hour history of generalized abdominal pain
fever (39 °C)
vomiting
constipation
a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness
soft stool without blood
C-reactive protein was elevated at 134.5 mg/L
air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops
a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops
a hyperdense midline mass above the bladder
normal hemoglobin, white-cell and platelet counts
normal prothrombin time, INR, glucose, creatinine, urea, sodium, and potassium

concepts.why: The presence of a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops and air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops suggests intussusception.
The symptoms of generalized abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting, along with the finding of a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness, are consistent with appendicitis.
The presence of a hyperdense midline mass above the bladder and a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops suggests a possible lymphoma.
The symptoms of abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting, along with the finding of a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness, are consistent with inflammatory bowel disease.
The presence of a hyperdense midline mass above the bladder and a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops suggests a possible ovarian tumor.

The presence of a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops and air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops suggests a possible Meckel's diverticulum.
The symptoms of abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting are consistent with gastroenteritis.
The symptoms of abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting, along with the finding of a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness, are consistent with mesenteric lymphadenitis.
